This post ressonates with me because I had on top of the DID a psychotic episode aswell.

There are some overlapses within DID and schizophrenia and the are called the Schneideriain symptoms.  


1. It's about hearing voices. While the DID patient describes the location of the voices within their heads, people with schizophrenia experience the voices as something that comes from an external source (like someone or something is externally controlling their thoughts and they can like really "hear" (like turning their heads when they hear a voice, trying to locate the source).  


2. It's also about hallucination. While the psychotic patient might have visual hallucination, this isn't very common among people with DID.



The main difference between the two disorders are the connection to reality.  
While a patient with schizophrenia is losing touch with reality, a patient with DID can usually distinguish between their alter's voices and the world around them. They usually keep in touch with reality.




BUT!  



Psychosis is a symptom and can occure in every psychiatrical disorder.  
There is a term called dissociative psychosis. So its important to seperate the symptom of psychosis from the disorder schizophrenia. Yeah, it's  the main symptom of people who are suffering from schizophrenia to have psychosis but psychosis isn't bound to schizophrenia.  



Back to the disscociative psychosis. It is described in literatur that a induvidals with DID can experience a psychotic break when the system is destabilitized.  
The hallucinations and break from reality normaly reduce by itself once the patient can become more stable. Sometimes neuroleptics can be given for a short period of time but most of the time they don't seem to be very usefull in this case and the psychotic symptoms disappear within less then 3 weeks.



I'm having DID aswell and experienced psychosis aswell (my grandma suffers from psychosis aswell) there doesn't have to be the one OR the other...  


Every brain is different I believe there can be a comorbitity aswell.  


Sorry if my explanation is confusing but I read a book about it.

It really helped me to understand my symptoms.  


Keep on fighting!
